built_with: thesis_v2/_slabtest.tex harness, pdflatex, preamble.tex loaded; no Overfull/Underfull boxes

drawn_to_scale.note: The two wedge AREAS in the main disc are the only scaled marks in the figure. Wedge area fraction = variance share, so wedge angle = share * 360 deg.

unshaded_remainder.derivation: 1 - context - drug_pure; the two subspaces are orthogonal so the shares add
unshaded_remainder.note: carries no printed number in the figure

cell_line_subspace.why_not_a_wedge: the cell-line subspace lies INSIDE the context subspace, so a third disjoint wedge would assert a partition the data do not support

cell_line_over_drug_pure_ratio.thesis_text: 04b-representation.tex:350 'On subspace fraction cell line measures 15--22x the purified slab'

one_mismatched_geometry.source: 07-Appendix.tex:520 and 04b-representation.tex:372, 'roughly 99.5% of the control's squared norm'
one_mismatched_geometry.how: an isotropic direction in 2048 dimensions puts, on average, 10/2048 = 0.0048828 of its squared norm in a 10-dimensional slab; the control arrow is drawn at 86 deg to the slab axis, cos^2(86 deg) = 0.004866, so the drawn angle carries the number

two_ablate_then_add.source: 07-Appendix.tex:456, 'the control delivers 5.3x the perturbation in 100% of draws'
two_ablate_then_add.bar_note: schematic, but internally consistent: delivered = added - removed = (2.00-1.25) - (1.70-1.25) = 0.30

three_the_normaliser.note: the four target ticks are drawn identically and depressed identically; the figure asserts uniformity, not any per-target magnitude

other_printed_integers.10: pure_drug_dims / raw_drug_dims = 10 at every layer; config n_dims = 10; 04b-representation.tex:259 'top ten orthonormal directions'
other_printed_integers.11: caption only: twelve centred class means span at most eleven directions, 04b-representation.tex:260
other_printed_integers.0.083: chance, caption only; workspace_probe.json chance = 0.08333333333333333, thesis table caption 04b-representation.tex:305 says 'chance is 0.083'
other_printed_integers.11.3: the slab wedge angle in degrees, stated in the caption; equals 0.031459 * 360
